A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Styl3R and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably despite added sections and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original stylization, consistency, runtime and novel-view-synthesis results, along with ablations and additional qualitative outputs in the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds human preferences, perceptual metrics and quantitative ablation results in Tables 3-5.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same structure and appearance branches, attention mechanisms, two-stage training, identity loss and progressive multi-view training. Appendix C mentions VGGT only as a possible future replacement, not an implemented component.

E1.justification: The scene/style datasets and reconstruction/stylization tasks remain unchanged. The new metrics and voting study evaluate the already covered RE10K and Tanks and Temples domains without introducing new documented input conditions or task requirements.

E2.justification: StyTr2 newly appears in reported Tanks and Temples comparisons in Tables 3-4; v1's corresponding Figure 4 compared Styl3R with ARF, StyleRF and StyleGaussian. The existing RE10K and novel-view-synthesis comparator sets remain intact.

E3.justification: v2 adds ArtFID and RGB-uv histogram evaluation plus an online study asking voters to select the most harmonious integration of style and scene. It reports 1,274 RE10K votes, 294 Tanks and Temples votes and 392 ablation votes. These substantially expand evaluation beyond the retained consistency and reconstruction protocols.

E4.justification: New Table 5 quantitatively supports the existing relu3_1 versus relu3_1+relu4_1 content-loss ablation using ArtFID, histogram scores and human preferences. The question tested and Figure 7 are retained; identity-loss and input-view-count ablations are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The new voting totals and percentages describe sample sizes and outcomes, without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 3-5 add substantial perceptual and preference results: Styl3R receives 53.29% of RE10K votes and 38.78% of Tanks and Temples votes, with ArtFID scores of 35.12 and 38.05. The two-layer content-loss variant receives 64.80% preference. Earlier consistency/runtime scores and NVS scores remain unchanged; v1's NVS Table 3 becomes v2's Table 6.

T1.justification: The mathematical model definitions, attention equation and training-loss equation are unchanged. The added evaluation metrics are cited without introducing new mathematical definitions, derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: instant stylization from sparse unposed images, separation of structure and appearance, preservation of reconstruction capability, and generalization across scenes and styles. New evaluations support these existing claims.

C2.justification: New Section 5 explicitly weighs single-pass speed and accessibility against optimization-based geometry quality and scalability, acknowledging training-data demands, lower reconstruction fidelity and memory constraints. Appendix C adds explicit view-count and resolution limitations and proposed remedies. This substantially expands the earlier limitations discussion, which chiefly identified static-scene support.

D1.justification: Model architecture, initialization, training resolution, hardware/time, optimizer and learning rates remain unchanged, as do Appendix A's xFormers, DPT and baseline-training details. Project and baseline-checkpoint access information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds HistoGAN and ArtFID as evaluation references and VGGT as a possible future backbone. Section 5 expands positioning against reconstruction-then-stylization pipelines, while the related-work survey and central novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 inserts a user-study paragraph, a Discussion section and Appendix C, renumbers the conclusion, and adds acknowledgements and the NeurIPS 2025 conference footer. These are localized structural additions; the abstract, introduction and method prose are essentially retained.

P2.justification: Three compact tables are added for preferences, perceptual metrics and ablation results, requiring local text reflow. The original NVS table is renumbered from 3 to 6. All fourteen figures, including the appendix galleries, retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: v1's quantitative evaluation primarily measured consistency and reconstruction, leaving stylistic quality supported mainly by visual examples. v2's perceptual metrics, human preferences and quantitative ablation directly strengthen evidence for this central claim. The new discussion also makes important practical tradeoffs explicit. Together these substantially improve validation and qualification, although missing participant, sampling and uncertainty details still limit the user study.
